subject: Packaging and SRE routing for StrataHealth VPC pilot
messages:
From: Alice Tan <alice@stratahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-04T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: VPC pilot: questions on packaging & SRE coverage

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to pilot Redwood's VPC deployment for a subset of our clinical inference traffic. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of two things before we circulate an internal SOW:  

1) How packaging is structured for a pilot vs. production (operator/node counts, platform fee expectations).
2) How oncall/SRE routing works — who is called first for Sev-1 vs. Sev-2, and how do escalation windows map to the platform fee?

Can you point me to a short doc or a concrete example we can share with our CFO and SRE? Also, procurement would like an initial target price band so they know whether to proceed with a 30-day pilot.

Appreciate it — happy to set a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Alice
Alice Tan
VP Product, StrataHealth
[Attachment: Strata_Initial_Requirements.xlsx (XLSX, 22 KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice@stratahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-04T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pilot: questions on packaging & SRE coverage

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the note and great to hear you're moving toward a pilot. I've attached a draft SOW and a short SLA matrix that maps severity levels to response windows and escalation hops. Quick answers up top:  

- Pilot packaging: typically 2 operator licenses (for your infra team) + a 4-node reserved pool for one month. Platform fee for a pilot is often treated as a timeboxed flat fee to cover private control plane and onboarding; we typically propose a 25% discount off the listed platform fee for pilots.
- Oncall/SRE routing: our runbook puts customer oncall first (if covered), then Redwood SRE as primary responder for platform faults. Sev-1: 15 minute acknowlege, 1 hour full response (RCAT), war room if not mitigated in 4 hours. Sev-2: 1 hour acknowledge, 8 hour remediation target.

I'll let Ben add the pricing bands and Marissa stitch in the procurement steps and signature path. Attaching: Strata_Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf and SLA_Matrix.xlsx — these are drafts we can redline.

Next steps: confirm pilot node sizing and we can issue a formal pilot quote and SOW. Would a 30-day pilot starting May 19th work for you?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Strategic Account Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Strata_Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 84 KB)]
[Attachment: SLA_Matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 12 KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-05T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pilot: questions on packaging & SRE coverage

Hi Alice / Kim —

Adding concrete bands so procurement has something to model:  

Option A — Pilot (30 days):
- 4-node reserved pool (r5-equivalent GPUs), operator license x2, timeboxed platform fee: $18k (pilot discounted from $24k list).
- Support: Business hours (Mon-Fri 8am-6pm PT) + Redwood oncall for platform escalations.

Option B — Pilot + 90-day extension path to prod:
- 8-node reserved pool, operator license x4, monthly platform fee upon conversion: $45k/month (we'd propose a 10% conversion credit applied to the first 3 invoices).
- Support: 24x7 SRE coverage for platform faults; application layer remains customer responsibility.

Notes on discounts: we can extend a 10% pilot-to-prod conversion credit (applied as a lump credit) or a straight 15% off the first 3 months' platform fee if you commit to a 12-month reserved capacity within 30 days of pilot completion.

Operational callouts: automatic KV-prefix caching reduces token costs for steady-state traffic; we can provide modeling if you share token/seq distribution.

If you like, I can push a formal quote into HubSpot (DEAL-6421) with the Option A/B breakdown and explicit redlines.

-ben
Ben Carter
Lead Commercials, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Pricing_Bands_Options.xlsx (XLSX, 9 KB)]

Subject: Re: VPC pilot: questions on packaging & SRE coverage

Thanks Ben — that's helpful. A couple of clarification requests from procurement/SRE before we proceed:  

- Procurement needs an explicit definition of "platform fault" vs. "application fault" so we can map liabilities and who pays for remediation hours. Could you add a short clause to the SOW that enumerates the boundaries?
- For the pilot we need the onboarding window in calendar days (how many days of SRE-led onboarding are included in the pilot fee?).
- On discounts: is the 10% conversion credit refundable against early termination or is it contingent on full 12-month consumption? We prefer credits that apply to invoices rather than cash refunds.

We can run the 30-day pilot but prefer the 4-node sizing to be validated by an initial run with a 2-day spike test. Can we schedule a technical sync next week (Alice + our SRE lead + Kimberly + Ben)?

On the legal side, procurement will ask for a DocuSign-ready SOW with tracked redlines.

Best,
Alice

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice@stratahealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-06T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pilot: questions on packaging & SRE coverage

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the detailed questions. A few concrete items to finalize so procurement can move to signature:  

1) Boundary language (to include in SOW):
- "Platform fault": failures of the Redwood control plane, model runtime crashes, network routing between Redwood-managed control plane and reserved pool, and issues caused by our quantization/runtime changes. Covered by Redwood support.
- "Application fault": bugs or performance issues in customer code, orchestration misconfigurations on customer infra, data schema mismatches. Customer owns remediation.

2) Onboarding window: pilot fee includes up to 10 business days of SRE-led onboarding and a 2-day spike validation test (we'll coordinate dates). Additional onboarding days billed at our professional services rate (listed in SOW).

3) Conversion credit: the 10% credit is applied as an account credit to invoices and is not refundable cash. It applies only if you convert to a 12-month committed reserved capacity within 30 days of pilot completion. We'll add exact language to the SOW so procurement can review.

Finally, to help legal/procurement, we've uploaded a DocuSign-ready SOW with tracked changes to the shared drive and pushed a draft quote to HubSpot (DEAL-6421). Links below. If that looks good, Kim — can you send the DocuSign link to Alice and procurement? We can do the technical sync on Tues May 13 at 10am PT; I'll invite Redwood's SRE lead.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if any item needs tightening.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
